title: Attend-and-Excite: Attention-Based Semantic Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
property: subject presence (attention peak of each subject word)
reads: SD1.4 cross-attention averaged over all 16x16 layers and heads, Softmax across tokens without start-of-text, Gaussian-smoothed map of each subject token
trained_on: nothing trained; hand-written loss L = max_s (1 - max A_t^s)
gradient_enters: z_t' = z_t - alpha_t grad_{z_t} L, alpha_t 20 decaying to 10, first 25 of 50 steps, refinement to peaks 0.05, 0.5, 0.8 with at most 20 updates, no normalisation or cap described
unseen: no: nothing is trained, so no category is held out
headline: Animal-Animal CLIP text-text similarity between prompt and BLIP caption (cosine, higher better): 0.806 for Attend-and-Excite against 0.767 for SD and 0.692 for Composable Diffusion; SD1.4
copy_or_avoid: Measure and raise the weakest word's attention peak before separating maps, because its loss works through word strength and our correlation push has no term for it (inferred)

quotes.text: We then consider the resulting crossattention map obtained after averaging all 16 × 16 attention layers and heads.
re-weigh the attention values by ignoring the attention of ⟨𝑠𝑜𝑡⟩ and performing a Softmax operation on the remaining tokens
filter used to smooth the cross-attention maps 𝐴𝑠𝑡 has a kernel size of 3 and a standard deviation of 𝜎 = 0.5
We use the official Stable Diffusion v1.4 text-to-image model
requires no additional training or fine-tuning
the loss attempts to strengthen the activations of the most neglected subject token at the current timestep
where 𝛼𝑡 is a scalar defining the step size of the gradient update.

We set the iterations to 𝑡 1 = 0, 𝑡 2 = 10, and 𝑡 3 = 20 with minimum required attention values of 𝑇1 = 0.05,𝑇2 = 0.5, and 𝑇3 = 0.8
